uganda_kob.name: Uganda kob
facts: The Uganda kob is Uganda's national antelope and appears on the country's coat of arms.
Male kobs compete for small territories called leks, where females come to choose a mate.
Kobs can run at high speed to escape predators such as lions and hyenas.

bird.name: Bird
facts: Uganda is home to over 1,000 recorded bird species, one of the richest bird diversities in Africa.
Many birds seen on safari gather near rivers and swamps, where food is easiest to find.
Bird calls and flight patterns can reveal when a larger predator is nearby.

chimpanzee.name: Chimpanzee
facts: Chimpanzees live in social groups and communicate through calls, gestures, and facial expressions.
They use tools, such as sticks and stones, to get food like insects and nuts.
Chimpanzees share about 98 percent of their DNA with humans, their closest living relatives.

elephant.name: African elephant
facts: Elephants are the largest land animals and can weigh as much as six tonnes.
They live in close family groups led by an older, experienced female.
Elephants use their trunks for breathing, smelling, drinking, and picking up objects.

gorilla.name: Gorilla
facts: Gorillas live in family groups led by one dominant adult male, called a silverback.
They are mostly plant eaters, spending much of the day feeding on leaves, stems, and fruit.
Gorillas are a critically endangered species, and Uganda is one of the few countries where they survive in the wild.

hippo.name: Hippopotamus
facts: Hippos spend most of the day in water and come onto land mainly at night to feed.
Despite their size, hippos can run faster than a human over short distances on land.
Hippos are considered one of the most dangerous animals in Africa due to their aggressive behaviour.

warthog.name: Warthog
facts: Warthogs use their snouts and tusks to dig for roots and bulbs in the ground.
They often shelter in abandoned burrows, usually ones dug by other animals such as aardvarks.
Warthogs can run quickly to escape danger and often live in small family groups.

ateso.back_translation: The warthog is the largest wild pig in Africa

tiger.name: Tiger
facts: Tigers are the largest of all cat species.
No two tigers have the same stripe pattern.
Tigers come from Asia and do not live wild in Africa; in Uganda they are seen at UWEC in Entebbe.
Unlike most cats, tigers like water and are strong swimmers.

leopard.name: Leopard
facts: Leopards live in many of Uganda's national parks, including Queen Elizabeth and Murchison Falls.
A leopard often carries its prey up into a tree to keep it away from lions and hyenas.
Leopards are mostly active at night and are very hard to spot by day.

fox.name: Fox
facts: Foxes belong to the dog family.
Their large ears help them hear small animals moving underground.
Foxes usually hunt alone rather than in packs.

frog.name: Frog or toad
facts: Frogs start life as tadpoles that live in water and breathe with gills.
Many frogs can take in oxygen through their skin.
The frog calls heard at night are mostly males calling to attract females.

snake.name: Snake
snake.safety: Do not approach: some snakes are venomous.
facts: Snakes have no eyelids and no external ears.
A snake flicks its tongue to collect scents from the air.
Uganda is home to pythons, cobras and vipers; the African rock python is Africa's largest snake.

fish.name: Fish
facts: Uganda shares Lake Victoria, Africa's largest lake, with Kenya and Tanzania.
Tilapia and Nile perch are important food fish in Uganda.
Fish breathe by taking oxygen from water through their gills.

zebra.name: Zebra
facts: Every zebra has its own unique stripe pattern.
In Uganda, zebras can be seen in Lake Mburo and Kidepo Valley National Parks.
Zebras live in family groups and often graze together with other grazing animals.

ateso.text: Ejaasi Zebra keda aiboisio nuegelegela nuka akwap

ateso.back_translation: Zebras have different habitats in the wild

monkey.name: Monkey
facts: Uganda has a great variety of primates; Kibale Forest alone has 13 primate species.
Monkeys have tails, which is one way to tell them apart from apes such as chimpanzees and gorillas.
Vervet monkeys use different alarm calls for different predators.

crocodile.name: Crocodile
crocodile.safety: Dangerous: stay away from the water's edge.
facts: The Nile crocodile is one of Africa's largest reptiles.
Many crocodiles can be seen along the Nile in Murchison Falls National Park.
Mother crocodiles carry their newly hatched young to the water in their mouths.

tortoise.name: Tortoise
facts: Some tortoises live for more than 100 years.
A tortoise's shell is part of its skeleton and cannot be taken off.
Tortoises live on land, while most turtles live in water.

giraffe.name: Giraffe
facts: The giraffe is the tallest land animal.
Uganda's giraffes are Rothschild's (Nubian) giraffes, found in Murchison Falls, Kidepo Valley and Lake Mburo.
A giraffe's long neck has the same number of bones (seven) as a human neck.

rhino.name: Rhinoceros
facts: Rhinos had disappeared from the wild in Uganda by the early 1980s.
They have been brought back at Ziwa Rhino Sanctuary, where they are protected and breeding.
A rhino's horn is made of keratin, the same material as human fingernails.

luganda.back_translation: The animal is called the Rhinoceros

squirrel.name: Squirrel
facts: Squirrels use their bushy tails for balance when climbing and jumping.
Many squirrels bury food to eat later.
Africa has both tree squirrels and ground squirrels.

lion.name: Lion
facts: The Ishasha sector of Queen Elizabeth National Park is famous for lions that climb and rest in trees.
Lions are the only cats that live in groups, called prides.
A lion's roar can be heard several kilometres away.

buffalo.name: African buffalo
facts: African buffaloes live in large herds that protect their young together.
They are considered one of the most dangerous animals in Africa, especially lone males.
Buffaloes are common in Queen Elizabeth and Murchison Falls National Parks.

cheetah.name: Cheetah
facts: The cheetah is the fastest land animal, reaching about 100 km/h in short sprints.
In Uganda, cheetahs are found mainly in Kidepo Valley National Park.
Cheetahs cannot roar; they chirp, purr and growl instead.

luganda.back_translation: A cheetah is a carnivorous animal

kudu.name: Kudu
facts: Male kudus have long spiral horns; only the males carry horns.
The thin white stripes on a kudu's body help it hide in bushes.
Kudus mostly eat leaves and shoots rather than grass.

kiswahili.text: Kudu ni mji wa Kenya katika Kaunti ya Kisii
kiswahili.auto_check: fail: a sentence, not a name
kiswahili.back_translation: Kudu is a town in Kenya in Kisii County

hyena.name: Hyena
facts: Spotted hyenas live in groups called clans, which are led by females.
Hyenas hunt much of their own food; they do not only scavenge.
The hyena's famous 'laugh' is a call it makes when excited or stressed.
